reviews.review:
This is a slog. I don't even know how or what I'm supposed to be doing most of the time and I'm still on the first major mission. The maps are too vague or obnoxious, and frankly is anyone else feeling like this is a borderlands ripoff?

Shepard, Garrus and the Normandy crew deserve a better legacy than this cash grab to come in after them.

UPDATE: I've never not finished a game, so I finished it. If you are a complete-ist, go for it, it's a gorgeous game to look at it. The heart is there. They just jammed it with so much stuff to do and not enough direction for me. Didn't cry once. For me that's a major point lost, especially after the story telling done in any single one of the original ME trilogy.

gameplay is fun and more diverse than the original ME games, allowing you to customize armor, weapons, and fighting style especially. the imagery is, for the most part, beautifully designed. from what i've heard, the main reasons that the original release of this game was poorly received was because of the lack of consistent direction and that the game was released before it was fully finished, causing several problems. but after updates, the game is fun and works quite well for me on both pc and ps4 (as someone who isn't very experienced with gaming, at least)

another thing people would say they disliked about the game was that you don't have the social reputation in-game that commander shepard did starting up in the original trilogy. mass effect andromeda's playable character, ryder, starts out as someone in their parent's shadow and as the game progresses, you build your reputation and start to become someone that people depend on/look up to, which i think is just as good of a story for your character because it's kinda the reverse of shepard's beginning.

After just playing through the remakes of the original trilogy... actually better than I remembered. Still not great, the open world can feel like "name a Ubisoft title", which is not amazing. The main story is super generic, but the companion banter and the feeling of being stranded in a new galaxy... actually sorta makes me feel like the Atlantis to the OG's SG1. Or it would if it was better in *every* way, sadly, while the combat and banter and overall tone is on point, the main story, and the "Ubisoft" maps bog it down. It was still overhated for it's time I think, and the combat is miles better, especially the vertical movement. Coming fresh from finishing the trilogy, I can see why it flopped. Coming back almost 8 years later after replaying the original via the Legendary Edition, it is actually, pretty fun.

Came for the hot aliens, stayed for the hot aliens.... I like aliens okay??  .... also, I enjoy the tone indicators in dialogue compared to ME3 but miss some of the tactical elements of ME3 (like the cover mechanics were better in ME3).
